item.description: Pope Leo XIV has summoned the leaders of the world’s episcopal conferences to the Vatican in October to discuss marriage and the family "in light of the changes that continue to impact families."

item.description: Pope Leo XIV declared Boys Town founder Father Edward Flanagan venerable, recognizing his heroic virtue and moving him one step closer to sainthood.

item.title: The case for a universal basic income in the era of A.I.
item.description: Do we just do nothing if artificial intelligence leads to rising unemployment and poverty?

item.title: Belgian bishop says he will 'make every effort' to ordain married men by 2028
item.description: In a pastoral letter published March 19, Bishop Johan Bonny of Antwerp wrote that the question is "no longer whether" married men can be ordained, but "when" and "who will do it."

item.title: Jerusalem patriarchate cancels Palm Sunday procession, postpones chrism Mass amid war
item.description: Uncertainty surrounds upcoming Holy Week liturgies — central to the Christian faith and typically drawing large gatherings of pilgrims and local worshippers.

item.title: Separating the art from the artist? Broadway’s ‘Giant’ wrestles with Roald Dahl’s antisemitism
item.description: The tragedy of Dahl’s antisemitism isn’t that it colored his art but that it clouded his vision and tainted his outrage.

item.title: Why do bad things happen to good people? A conversation on suffering with Kate Bowler
item.description: Kate Bowler leans, as I do, on a God who accompanies us through our suffering, as she felt God did during her cancer treatments.

item.title: On immigration and war, the U.S. bishops are echoing Oscar Romero
item.description: Decades after his martyrdom, Romero’s insistence that the laws of God stand above law created by humankind and the edicts and commands of political and military leaders has been repeated by bishops in the United States, speaking against war-making and mass deportation.

item.title: ‘Your homework is to tell someone you love them today’: Colman McCarthy’s lessons in peace
item.description: Colman McCarthy, who died on Feb. 27 at the age of 87, had a well-deserved reputation for seeking out the underdogs in life—as well as for his determined lifelong stands against war, capital punishment, homelessness and the other seamy sides of contemporary capitalism.

item.title: Report refutes abuse cover-up claims against Pope John Paul II as leader of Krákow archdiocese
item.description: "Our research shows that Cardinal Karol Wojtyla did not transfer priests from parish to parish when he learned of their criminal activities, but he took quick action, and some of his decisions were above-standard for the time," the March 13 report's lead said.

item.title: Archbishop Fulton Sheen to be beatified Sept. 24 in St. Louis
item.description: “Archbishop Fulton Sheen was one of the greatest voices of evangelization in the Church and the world in the 20th century,” Bishop Louis Tylka of Peoria said.

item.title: Pope Leo taps Australian church lawyer as Vatican’s chief legal expert
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has filled one of the most important Vatican vacancies by tapping Bishop Anthony Randazzo, an Australian church lawyer, to serve as the Holy See’s chief legal expert.
